$comment: Cases for the heartbeat site rule (design §4). When a heartbeat, event or exception verdict is due, the prober first asks whether the site itself is up: a missed job during an outage is the outage, not a second page. Note the probe branch — if the site's critical monitors were last seen up, or their last result is stale, the prober spends one extra request to find out before judging. That request is only made in the case that actually matters.

signal.last_ping_at: when this heartbeat last pinged, or null
signal.timeout_minutes: how long a start may go unfinished (event only)

site.critical_status: the last known status of the site's critical monitors: up, down, or stale
site.down_since: when the site's critical monitors first failed, or null
site.recovered_at: when they last came back, or null

input.extranet_reachable: whether the prober can currently reach this tenant's hub

actions.probe-then-judge: check the site's critical monitors now, then re-enter this function with the fresh status
actions.deliver: send the verdict in the next heartbeat delivery
actions.suppress: no verdict; report it in the suppressed[] list so the hub attaches it to the open incident
actions.hold: reach no conclusion yet; re-evaluate on a later sweep

cases.name: overdue, site last seen up
cases.note: Last seen up is not good enough to page on. The prober confirms with a live probe first, because the likeliest reason a job stopped pinging is that the whole site went down a moment ago.

cases.name: overdue, probe confirmed the site is up
cases.note: The web tier answers but the scheduler or queue did not. That is a real verdict and the one this whole rule exists to protect.

cases.name: overdue, site is known down
cases.note: No probe: the site's critical monitors failed recently and the status is fresh, so there is nothing to find out.

cases.name: overdue, site recovered less than one interval plus grace ago
cases.note: The queue has not had time to catch up yet. Judging here would page for an outage that is already over.

cases.name: still overdue more than one interval plus grace after recovery
cases.note: The web tier came back and the scheduler did not. A real verdict.

cases.name: overdue, extranet unreachable
cases.note: If the prober cannot reach the hub at all, it treats every one of that tenant's heartbeats as site-down. Undeliverable results plus a site actually down is what triggers the emergency contacts; a missed heartbeat is not.

cases.name: event failed explicitly while the site is up
cases.note: An explicit /fail ping needs no probe: the site clearly answered, because it just told us something broke.

cases.name: event started and never finished inside its timeout
a heartbeat that was missing pings again
cases.note: Recovery is delivered even if the site is down, so the hub can close the heartbeat's own state cleanly.
